nonex: It does NOT mean to stop when it gets hard.
It does NOT mean to take a shortcut.
vocab.example: The student had to persevere to learn all the spelling words.
vocab.starter: I had to persevere when _______ ...
vocab.why: Persevere is a powerful word about never giving up on your goals!

sentences.orig: the ferm in the forest grows berds nest fern plants

corr.e: The first word of a sentence must be capitalized.
Fern is spelled with 'er' not 'er-m.' The r-controlled vowel 'er' makes the 'er' sound.
Bird's needs an apostrophe to show the nest belongs to the bird, and 'ir' not 'er.'
Grows is the correct present tense verb for one farm.
A statement must end with a period.

sentences.fixed: The fern in the forest grows bird's nest fern plants.

pos.q: Find the article at the start of the sentence.
Find the first common noun for a type of plant.
Find the preposition that tells where.
Find the article before 'forest.'
Find the noun for a place with many trees.
Find the verb meaning to get bigger or to raise plants.
Find the possessive word meaning 'belonging to a bird.'
Find the noun for a bird's home.
Find the second noun for the type of plant.
Find the plural noun for living things that grow.

manip.task: Replace the noun 'forest' with a different place noun.
examples: The fern in the garden grows bird's nest fern plants.
The fern in the jungle grows bird's nest fern plants.

vocab.def: To go through something difficult without giving up.
vocab.simple: Endure means to keep going even when something is really hard or lasts a long time!
nonex: It does NOT mean to enjoy something fun.
It does NOT mean to avoid a challenge.
vocab.example: The plants endure the cold winter and bloom again in spring.
vocab.starter: I had to endure _______ but it was worth it because ...
vocab.why: Endure is a strong word for describing toughness and not giving up!

sentences.orig: the happy children sang songs at the summer party today

corr.e: The first word of a sentence must be capitalized.
Happy is the correct adjective in the subject part of the sentence.
Sang is the correct past tense of 'sing.' It is in the predicate part of the sentence.
Songs is a correct plural noun in the predicate.
A statement must end with a period.

sentences.fixed: The happy children sang songs at the summer party today.

pos.q: Find the article at the start of the subject.
Find the adjective in the subject that describes the children.
Find the noun in the subject — who the sentence is about.
Find the main verb that starts the predicate — what the children did.
Find the plural noun in the predicate for what they sang.
Find the preposition that tells where.
Find the article before 'summer.'
Find the word that describes the type of party.
Find the noun for a fun gathering.
Find the adverb that tells when.

manip.task: Replace the verb 'sang' with a different action verb.
examples: The happy children played songs at the summer party today.
The happy children performed songs at the summer party today.

vocab.def: To find and name something or someone.
vocab.simple: Identify means to point out what something is, like naming a bird you see!
nonex: It does NOT mean to make something up.
It does NOT mean to hide something.
vocab.example: Can you identify the subject and predicate in this sentence?
vocab.starter: I can identify _______ by looking at ...
vocab.why: Identify is a thinking word you use when finding and naming parts of a sentence!

sentences.orig: my best frend and i will visit the zoo tomorrow

corr.e: The first word of a sentence must be capitalized.
Friend is spelled with 'ie' not just 'e.'
And is the correct conjunction connecting two subjects.
The pronoun 'I' must always be capitalized, even in the middle of a sentence.
A statement must end with a period.

sentences.fixed: My best friend and I will visit the zoo tomorrow.

pos.q: Find the possessive word that starts the subject.
Find the adjective that describes the friend.
Find the first noun in the subject.
Find the conjunction that connects two subjects.
Find the pronoun that is the second subject.
Find the helping verb that starts the predicate.
Find the action verb in the predicate.
Find the article before 'zoo.'
Find the noun in the predicate for a place with animals.
Find the adverb in the predicate that tells when.

manip.task: Replace the noun 'zoo' with a different place noun.
examples: My best friend and I will visit the museum tomorrow.
My best friend and I will visit the aquarium tomorrow.

vocab.def: To know or remember something or someone you have seen before.
vocab.simple: Recognize means to see something and know what it is because you have seen it before!
nonex: It does NOT mean to see something for the first time.
It does NOT mean to guess wildly.
vocab.example: I can recognize the subject and predicate in every sentence now.
vocab.starter: I can recognize _______ because I have seen it ...
vocab.why: Recognize helps you talk about knowing things you have learned before!

sentences.orig: she dont want to give the book to he now

corr.e: The first word of a sentence must be capitalized.
Use 'doesn't' with 'she' and add an apostrophe for the contraction of 'does not.'
Give is the correct verb meaning to hand something to someone.
Use 'him' as the object pronoun after 'to.' 'He' is only used as a subject.
A statement must end with a period.

sentences.fixed: She doesn't want to give the book to him now.

pos.q: Find the subject pronoun for a girl.
Find the contraction that means 'does not.'
Find the verb meaning to wish for something.
Find the first preposition before 'give.'
Find the verb meaning to hand something to someone.
Find the article before 'book.'
Find the common noun for something you read.
Find the second preposition before 'him.'
Find the object pronoun for a boy.
Find the adverb that tells when.

manip.task: Replace the object pronoun 'him' with a different object pronoun.
examples: She doesn't want to give the book to her now.
She doesn't want to give the book to them now.

vocab.def: To look at or study something again.
vocab.simple: Review means to go back and look at something one more time to remember it better!
nonex: It does NOT mean to learn something new.
It does NOT mean to throw work away.
vocab.example: Let us review all the grammar rules we learned this year.
vocab.starter: I need to review _______ so I can ...
vocab.why: Review is an important study word for going over what you have learned!

sentences.orig: yesterday the teecher asked us to rite a storey about spring

corr.e: The first word of a sentence must be capitalized.
Teacher is spelled with 'ea' not 'ee.' The vowel team 'ea' makes the long 'e' sound here.
Write is spelled w-r-i-t-e. 'Rite' is a different word meaning a ceremony.
Story is spelled s-t-o-r-y. A 'storey' means a floor of a building.
A statement must end with a period.

sentences.fixed: Yesterday the teacher asked us to write a story about spring.

pos.q: Find the adverb that tells when.
Find the article before 'teacher.'
Find the common noun for a person who teaches.
Find the past tense verb meaning to request.
Find the object pronoun meaning 'our group.'
Find the preposition before 'write.'
Find the verb meaning to put words on paper.
Find the article before 'story.'
Find the noun for a tale with characters and events.
Find the preposition that tells the topic.
Find the noun for the season after winter.

manip.task: Replace the noun 'spring' with a different season or topic.
examples: Yesterday the teacher asked us to write a story about summer.
Yesterday the teacher asked us to write a story about animals.

vocab.def: To show how to do something or prove something is true.
vocab.simple: Demonstrate means to show others how something works or how to do it!
nonex: It does NOT mean to keep something a secret.
It does NOT mean to watch someone else do it.
vocab.example: The student will demonstrate her writing skills by reading her story aloud.
vocab.starter: I can demonstrate _______ by showing ...
vocab.why: Demonstrate is a powerful word for showing what you know and can do!
